name: Abigail Potter
outcome: not filed - a face exists and cannot be tied to her
detail: The 2016 Talisman carries an underclassman portrait cell printed ABBY POTTER on p. 285 (grid position row 2, column 1; PDF page 144, xref 18221, 510x510), and Abby is the ordinary short form of Abigail. It was not cut, because the Herald shows more than one Abby Potter at WKU in these years and the underclassman cell fits the wrong one. The Herald of 16 April 2015 has 'Bowling Green senior Abby Potter, Greek Week chair and Kappa Delta sorority member', a junior in its stories of 19 March and 3 April 2014, so that Abby Potter graduated in spring 2015 and cannot be an underclassman in a book made in 2015-16. A photojournalism major' - she was an undergraduate in 2015-16 and fits the cell. Nothing in the Judicial Council record gives a major, a hometown or a class year that would separate them. The Herald names the justice twice, on 17 and 21 April 2015, both times as 'Judicial Council member Abby Potter' quoted on the Richey election appeal, and photographs her neither time.

name: Abdullah Raza
outcome: a frame exists, the person is named, and which face is his cannot be settled - WITHHELD, crop staged
detail: WORKLIST, not officers. The 2016 Talisman indexes 'Raza, Abdullah 221' and printed page 221 carries a 3492x3492 full-page photograph of the Pakistani Student Association in a huddle before a cricket match, captioned 'Sialkot, Pakistan, junior Abdullah Raza brings the Pakistani Student Association together for a cricket match against the Indian Student Association at Lampkin Park.' The caption names one person and the frame holds at least six, arms across shoulders. One man is central, sharp, facing the camera and mid-shout, and the composition and the verb both point at him, but the caption gives no position and the archive's own register has refused the same shape of claim before, on Beth McGrew's garden-party frame and on Murphy Burke's forum frame. Withheld on that precedent rather than published on a reading of the composition. The crop is staged at ~/Desktop/SGA60 photo hunt/n1419/UNRESOLVED-2016-17-abdullah-raza--talisman-p221-central-figure.jpg so the work is not lost; publish it only if a second frame or a positional caption turns up. Two facts in its favour if anyone revisits it: the caption gives him a home town, Sialkot, Pakistan, and a class year, junior in 2015-16, which the archive does not otherwise have; and Omer Toqeer, whose portrait was found on this run, was the Pakistani Student Association's president in the same year, so the two SGA senators were in the same society.
